title: The Passage of the Coral Triangle
premise: Salvage diver Lena Lockridge is hired to recover equipment from a wreck in the Coral Triangle that the navy officially denies exists. When a government survey team vanishes from the same waters, leaving their gear intact and no tracks, Lena and her crew are conscripted to find them — and discover the team stumbled onto a sunken cache of evidence implicating officials in a decade-old atrocity. Hunted by the people who buried the truth, Lena must lead her crew across the archipelago ahead of the monsoon, choosing between selling out for survival or exposing herself to deliver justice no court will touch. In the end she trades her anonymity — the identity she built to escape her past — to put the evidence in the world's hands, surviving the crossing but losing the life she had.
about_author: Bram Halloran is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent six years running supply routes through Southeast Asia before turning to writing full-time. He lives on a restored trawler and writes about the sea's capacity to both hide and reveal what people would rather forget.

chapters.title: Twelve Miles Deep
chapters.summary: Lena Lockridge dives a charted wreck off Sulawesi and finds cargo manifests that shouldn't exist, stamped with dates from an incident the navy scrubbed twelve years ago. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in the careful, rootless life she has measured in nautical miles rather than years.

chapters.title: The Client Who Pays in Silence
chapters.summary: A government fixer named Okafor hires Lena's crew to salvage gear abandoned by a vanished survey team, insisting there are no bodies and no questions. Her engineer, Devi, smells a trap; her captain, Ruiz, needs the money. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: reluctant complicity as greed and curiosity outweigh instinct.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: On the survey camp's island, everything remains — laptops, food stores, even shoes by the tents — but no tracks lead anywhere. Devi recovers a corrupted drive fragment mentioning 'the Ledger.' POV: Devi. Emotional beat: creeping dread; absence more frightening than violence.

chapters.title: Wake in the Dark
chapters.summary: A black-hulled boat shadows them through the night passage; Ruiz runs dark and loses it in fishing traffic, but not before photographing its registration — a hull decommissioned two years ago. POV: Ruiz. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance; he decides they're already targets.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Devi restores the drive: the survey team found a sealed container shipwreck holding documents proving officials orchestrated the atrocity twelve years ago and silenced witnesses — including, Lena realizes with horror, people from her own buried past. POV: Devi. Emotional beat: revelation as burden; knowledge becomes danger.

chapters.title: What Lena Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Lena's real name, her role as a junior analyst whose report was used to cover the incident, and her flight into diving and assumed identity. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: shame surfacing; the miles she traveled were escape, not freedom.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: Okafor boards them at a fuel stop, offers triple pay to hand over the drive and forget the survey team, hinting he knows who Lena used to be. She stalls. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus the first pull toward justice outside any law.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Clock
chapters.summary: Ruiz lays out the brutal math: only one viable route across the archipelago reaches neutral press contacts before the dry season ends and the storms seal the straits. It passes through waters controlled by a pirate fleet. POV: Ruiz. Emotional beat: grim resolve; the crossing becomes a race against weather and hunters alike.

chapters.title: Smoke Over Ambon
chapters.summary: Resupply port ambush — men searching boats for the crew. They slip out during a dock fire of uncertain origin, gaining a day but burning their spare parts and a friendship with a harbor contact who pays for it. POV: Devi. Emotional beat: guilt; survival now has visible costs.

chapters.title: The Pirate Toll
chapters.summary: The fleet intercepts them. Their leader, Sari, turns out to be a survivor of the atrocity; when Devi shows her the Ledger, the toll becomes an alliance — but Sari demands Lena's truth in exchange. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: exposure; confessing her old name to strangers and being spared anyway.

chapters.title: Convoy of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sari's boats escort them through the hunters' patrol line using decoy lights and reef channels only smugglers know. One of her people dies covering their escape. POV: Ruiz. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude; the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Sea
chapters.summary: Storm-bound at a hidden anchorage, the crew argues: sell the drive, leak it, or bury it. Devi wants justice, Ruiz wants everyone alive, and Lena admits the documents also indict her own silence. POV: alternating crew voices via dialogue. Emotional beat: fracture and honesty; the theme of identity laid bare.

chapters.title: The Survey Team Found
chapters.summary: Sari's scouts locate three survey members alive, held in a coastal compound awaiting extraction by the same people hunting Lena. Rescuing them means revealing their route. POV: Devi. Emotional beat: moral escalation — witnesses can't be left behind if justice is to mean anything.

chapters.title: Compound Night
chapters.summary: A night raid frees the surveyors; Lena comes face to face with Okafor's superior, who offers her full restoration of her old career in exchange for the drive. She refuses — aloud, for the first time choosing who she is over who she was. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: climax of identity; refusal as rebirth.

chapters.title: Running the Straits
chapters.summary: Full pursuit. The crew threads a typhoon-fringed strait with the freed surveyors aboard, engines failing, Devi improvising repairs under fire while Ruiz navigates by dead reckoning. POV: Devi. Emotional beat: white-knuckle competence; the crew becoming a single organism.

chapters.title: What the Storm Takes
chapters.summary: The storm catches them. A hunter vessel sinks; so does Sari's flagship with half her fleet. Lena dives into collapsing seas to pull survivors — including the man sent to kill her. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: mercy as choice; the sea strips everyone to equals.

chapters.title: The Prisoner
chapters.summary: The rescued hunter, Vasquez, reveals the operation's scope and where the final evidence chain must be delivered to be unstoppable — and warns that Okafor has gone rogue, planning to sink the story and everyone carrying it. POV: Vasquez. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; enemy turned mirror.

chapters.title: Last Port Before the Rains
chapters.summary: They reach the press contact's island hours before the season's first true storm front. But Okafor's boat is already anchored offshore, waiting to trade: the surveyors' lives for the drive. POV: Ruiz. Emotional beat: cornered calm; Ruiz prepares to gamble everything on a bluff.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ruiz bluffs Okafor into believing copies exist in three hands; Sari's remaining boats surface in support. Okafor overreaches, his own superiors disavow him via intercepted orders, and his crew stands down. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: tension breaking into triumph earned by nerve, not firepower.

chapters.title: Handover
chapters.summary: The Ledger goes to journalists and the surviving survey team testifies remotely from the island. Lena gives her real name on record, dissolving the identity she hid behind for twelve years. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law finally entering the law.

chapters.title: After the Snows of Rain
chapters.summary: Investigations begin; some guilty fall, many don't. Sari rebuilds, Vasquez disappears into testimony protection, and Okafor faces a tribunal he once managed for others. POV: Devi. Emotional beat: sober satisfaction; imperfect justice still worth its price.

chapters.title: Miles, Then Years
chapters.summary: Lena returns to the first wreck with a new charter, diving not to escape but to document, measuring time in seasons now instead of miles. Ruiz asks where next; she names a place she's never been. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — survival paid for, identity chosen, horizon open.
